text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Sofia city court rejected the Bulgarian National Bank's insolvency suit against First Private Bank.
-- Fuel prices in Bulgaria will not be revised before Christmas, a senior Price Committee official said.
-- Deputy prime minister Doncho Konakchiev agreed with his visiting Russian counterpart Oleg Lobov to facilitate imports of some 150,000 tonnes of Russian grain in exchange for Bulgarian medicines.
-- Bulgaria's Agency for Economic Forecast and Development said it expected annual inflation of 20 to 30 percent if a currency board system is introduced.
-- Bulgaria's ambassador to Peru Dimitar Stanoev was taken hostage together with other 250 people by leftist guerrillas in the residence of the Japanese ambasador in Lima.

-- Bulgaria's trade unions agreed with the Bulgarian Economic Chamber (BEC) to pay wages in state companies weekly, daily, and hourly to protect employees' interests if a currency board system is not introduced and Bulgaria faces hyperinflation, a BEC senior official said.
-- Deputies of the opposition Bulgarian Business Bloc said they had submited a draft law in parliament to cut Value Added Tax on newspapers and books to 3 percent from 22 percent.
-- The state energy regulation committee discussed a proposal to raise electricity charges by some 20 percent from January 1, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- Food prices in Bulgaria have risen by 330 percent since the beginning of the year, Bulgaria's Consumer Federation figures showed.
